23 An observer is standing on a railway platform. A train passes the observer at constant speed
while emitting sound of constant frequency f from its whistle.
What does the observer hear?
A
sound of a decreasing frequency as the train approaches and of an increasing frequency as
it moves away
B
sound of a higher frequency than f as the train approaches and of a lower frequency than f
as the train moves away
C
sound of a lower frequency than f as the train approaches and of a higher frequency than f
as the train moves away
D
sound of an increasing frequency as the train approaches and as it moves away

hints: Notice the question states constant train speed and constant emitted frequency $f$, so compare only approaching versus moving away.
Recall that sound wavefronts bunch together in front of a moving source and spread out behind it, changing observed wavelength $\lambda_o$.
Use $v = f_o \lambda_o$ with constant sound speed $v$ to link shorter $\lambda_o$ on approach to higher $f_o$, and longer $\lambda_o$ on recession to lower $f_o$.
walkthrough: Identify the set-up: stationary observer, source moving at constant speed, true whistle frequency $f$ constant.
State the Doppler rule for sound: motion of source toward observer compresses wavefronts, motion away stretches them.
On approach, observed wavelength $\lambda_o$ is less than true wavelength $\lambda$, so with $f_o = v/\lambda_o$ the heard frequency is constant and greater than $f$.
After passing, the source moves away, $\lambda_o$ is greater than $\lambda$, so $f_o = v/\lambda_o$ is constant and less than $f$.
There is a sudden drop from high to low pitch at passing, not a continuous glide, because speed is constant. This is option B.

A.explanation: The observed frequency does not slide down on approach and up on recession - the shift is steady while approaching and steady while receding.

B.explanation: Wavefronts are compressed ahead of the approaching train and stretched behind the receding train, giving observed frequency above $f$ then below $f$.

C.explanation: This reverses the Doppler shift - approach compresses the waves to higher frequency, not lower frequency.

D.explanation: At constant train speed the observed frequency is constant during approach and constant during recession, not continuously increasing.
